title: Deployment-aware regression decisioning PRD for Optimize evals
creator: Amrita Shah
description: PRD to define concrete evaluation and decisioning requirements for Optimize so rollouts can be deployed with deployment-aware A/B gating and automated rollback triggers. The doc covers prompt set design across cohorts, multi-metric regression thresholds, weighted A/B pass/fail rules, and an actionable decision tree that integrates telemetry from Console. Goal: reduce manual review surface by 70% and ensure safe automated rollback for high-risk regressions.
background: Current Optimize eval work defines static regression thresholds and runbooks but lacks deployment context (e.g., dedicated vs hosted, latency-sensitive cohorts) and clear automated actions. Multiple incidents showed late detection of quality regressions when models were rolled across regions. This PRD ties evaluation signals to deployment policies and specifies acceptance criteria for canaries, staggered rollouts, and automatic failover.
scope: IN SCOPE: prompt set composition guidance for cohort stratification, definition of primary/secondary metrics (accuracy, hallucination rate, latency tail, token cost), statistical tests and minimum sample sizes, thresholding/weighting rules for composite signals, deterministic rollback triggers and severity tiers, console UI hooks for flagged runs, and telemetry schema updates. OUT OF SCOPE: model training changes, full CI integration, pricing changes.
out_of_scope: Model retraining pipelines, infra autoscaling policies (except where noted for telemetry), and long-term model registry workflows.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Prompt set spec: for each customer cohort there is a documented seed set (>=500 examples where feasible) + stratified sampling recipe covering 3 axes: intent, difficulty, domain. Sample recipes exist for chat, completion, and embeddings.

A2: Metrics: primary composite signal defined as weighted sum of normalized metrics: quality_accuracy (50%), hallucination_rate (30%), latency_p95 (10%), token_cost_delta (10%). Weights must be configurable per release.

A3: Statistical tests: per-cohort A/B comparisons use bootstrap confidence intervals with alpha=0.01 for primary signal and minimum N=200 per cohort; when sample sizes are below minimum, gating will mark as 'insufficient' rather than pass.

A4: Regression thresholds: default fail thresholds are set at >3% absolute drop in primary signal or >5% relative increase in hallucination_rate for high-impact cohorts. Thresholds are documented and can be overridden with approval.

A5: Canary policy: automated canary runs must pass primary signal at 99% CI and show no degradation on secondary metrics for 48 hours before 10% traffic shift. Rollouts must support staggered ramp with automatic pause on fail.

A6: Automated rollback triggers: clear mapping of signal -> action. Example: primary signal drop >5% OR hallucination increase >8% -> immediate rollback to previous pinned model and alert to on-call. Less severe breaches trigger pause + human review workflow within Console.
A7: Console integration: UI shows per-cohort pass/fail status, signal breakdown, sample counterexamples, and one-click rollback with audit log entry and link to PR/commit.
A8: Test coverage: synthetic evaluation harness in repo runbook passes end-to-end for at least two model variants and demonstrates rollback flow in staging.
A9: Runbook and run cadence: evaluation job schedule and on-call playbook documented with owner and SLAs for investigation timeline (15m triage, 2h mitigation plan, 24h RCA).
A10: Monitoring: telemetry keys and dashboards created in Console with alerting thresholds defined and smoke tests validating alerts fire on injected fault signals.
A11: Documentation: PRD, sample prompt sets, and step-by-step acceptance checklist stored in Drive alongside links to demo recordings.
A12: Stakeholder sign-off: PM, Eng, Design, Security, and Solutions each leave a review comment in the PRD and approve the rollout plan.
A13: Rollback audit: every automated rollback produces an audit entry that includes the top contributing signals and the sample counterexamples used by the decisioning engine.
A14: Minimal false positive tolerance: rate of automated rollback false positives must be <1% across a 30-day synthetic validation in staging.
decision_log: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting. Decision: use composite weighted signal rather than single metric to reduce noisy rollbacks. Action: ENG to prototype telemetry schema.
2025-02-17: PM/Eng trade-off review. Decision: require minimum sample sizes (N>=200) to avoid spurious CI pass/fail. Action: iterate on sampling recipes for low-volume customers.
2025-02-19: Design review. Decision: Console must show counterexamples and a confidence band for each metric. Action: DES to deliver mocks (DES-2102).
2025-02-20: Security input. Decision: no encryption changes required; audit trail must be write-once and accessible to SOC. Action: ENG to add audit KV to schema.
tradeoffs: Favoring safety by conservative thresholds increases human review overhead for marginal changes. We accept slightly slower rollouts for lower false positive rollback risk.
Using composite signals reduces single-metric noise but can obscure root cause; mitigation: show metric-level contributions and counterexamples in Console.
Setting strict sample minimums delays gating for low-volume cohorts; mitigation: mark 'insufficient data' and require manual review rather than auto-pass.
Automated rollback reduces time-to-mitigation but risks churning customer traffic. Mitigation: tiered rollback (pause -> partial rollback -> full rollback) with explicit thresholds.
risks: Insufficient prompt set coverage for niche domains leading to blindspots.
Telemetry or schema mismatches across Dedicated/Private deployments preventing consistent gating.
Overly aggressive automated rollback causing customer-facing availability issues.
Statistical tests misapplied to non-iid prompt samples creating false alarms.
Engineering bandwidth constraints for end-to-end test harness and Console integration.
next_steps: Finalize prompt set sampling recipes and publish canonical seed sets for three customer archetypes: consumer-chat, enterprise-search, support-bot.
ENG to implement telemetry schema and CI job to compute composite signal in staging (ETA 2 weeks).
DES to deliver Console mocks and microcopy for risk states (ETA 1 week).
Schedule cross-functional review on 2025-02-28 for sign-off and pilot launch plan.
